organization: Illinois General Assembly / JCAR (77 Ill. Adm. Code 245.95)
title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code - Section 245.95 Licensure fees
claim: Home services agency license fee not to exceed $1,500 annually (non-refundable); home services placement agency fee not to exceed $500; IDPH renewal form lists $1,500; IDPH FAQ says provisional license decision within ~90 days.
excerpt: Paraphrase: a home services agency shall pay a licensure fee not to exceed $1,500 annually; placement agency not to exceed $500.
limitations: Fee read via search summary of rule text and IDPH renewal form; confirm current text before filing.

title: FY26 Enacted Budget (Public Act 104-0003)
claim: Community Care Program (CCP) FY26 budget ~$1.6B; in-home services rate increased from $29.63 to $30.80/hour effective 1 Jan 2026; projected caseload growth 4% and utilization +9%.
excerpt: Rate increase as of January 1, 2026 for In-Home Services from $29.63 to $30.80
limitations: Budget presentation, not the rate rule itself. HB4662 proposing $33.92/hr from 2027 (with $20.75/hr worker wage floor) was in committee as of March 2026.

organization: Home Instead, Inc. (FDD Item 19, third-party hosted extract)
title: Home Instead 2025 Franchise Disclosure Document - Item 19 Financial Performance Representations (FY2024 data)
claim: 603 U.S. franchised units: average 2024 gross sales $2,609,616, median $2,261,503; average client hours 78,428 (implies ~$33 gross sales per client hour). Units with 1-2 yr tenure: 4 of 5 under $500k; 3-4 yr tenure: 9 of 14 at $1.0-1.5M. No cost/profit data disclosed.
excerpt: 603 ... Average Gross Sales $2,609,616 ... Median Gross Sales Per Franchised Business $2,261,503
limitations: Hosted by a third-party aggregator (r2.dev), not a state FDD database; gross sales only, no expenses; closed units excluded (survivorship); mature units dominate (65% have 16+ yrs tenure).

organization: Addus HomeCare (earnings call transcript via Motley Fool)
title: Addus HomeCare Q4 2025 earnings call transcript (call held 24 Feb 2026)
claim: Incumbent economics: Q4 2025 gross margin 32.8% (personal-care heavy); Illinois (largest personal care market) 3.9% rate increase 1 Jan 2026 worth ~$17.5M annualized with margins 'in the low 20% range'; Illinois DSO 54.7 days in Q4 vs 32.5 in Q3; management expects 80/20 rule to be eliminated.
excerpt: Margins are "consistent in the low 20% range." ... Illinois DSO rose to 54.7 days from 32.5 days
limitations: Transcript partly machine-produced; incumbent at scale, not new-entrant economics; gross margin is before G&A.

organization: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
title: Non-Emergency Transportation (provider page) and IMPACT high-risk provider page
claim: Transdev is the contact/prior-approval administrator for fee-for-service NEMT (netspap.com); MCO members' transport handled via MCO subcontractors; providers enroll via IMPACT (Atypical Agency for medicar/service car/taxi); HFS classifies NEMT providers as high-risk for screening.
excerpt: Paraphrase: questions about FFS customers go to Transdev (netspap.com); MCO customers handled via MCO subcontractor lists and dispute processes.
limitations: Page lists no rates; high-risk classification from HFS IMPACT page via search summary.

organization: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
title: Public notice: NEMT rate increase per PA 102-1037
claim: Effective 1 Jan 2023, HFS increased Medicar base and attendant rates and service-car base rates; ~$20M/yr added spend across FFS and MCO.
excerpt: will increase both the base rate and the attendant's rate for Medicar providers, as well as increase the base rate for service car providers
limitations: Dollar rates are in the HFS Transportation fee schedule, not retrieved.

title: A Closer Look at the Work Requirement Provisions in the 2025 Federal Budget Reconciliation Law (and KFF allocation of CBO estimates)
claim: 2025 reconciliation law (OBBBA) requires Medicaid work requirements for expansion adults by 1 Jan 2027 (extensions possible); CBO-based federal Medicaid reductions ~$911B over 10 yrs incl. provider-tax limits (~$191B) and state-directed-payment limits (~$149B).
excerpt: Paraphrase: states must condition expansion-adult eligibility on work requirements by January 1, 2027.
limitations: Secondary analysis of statute/CBO; Illinois-specific impact not quantified here.

title: CY 2026 Home Health PPS Final Rule (CMS-1828-F) fact sheet
claim: Net -1.3% (~$220M) aggregate Medicare home health payment change for CY2026; same rule restarts DMEPOS competitive bidding with next round to begin no later than 1 Jan 2028.
excerpt: Paraphrase: aggregate 1.3% decrease in Medicare home health payments; next DMEPOS competitive bidding round no later than January 1, 2028.
limitations: Read through search summaries of CMS fact sheet and Federal Register; product categories for next CBP round not confirmed.

title: The State of HCBS in 2026; LeadingAge notes on Access Rule 80/20
claim: CMS 2024 Access Rule 80/20 provision (80% of Medicaid personal care/homemaker payments to direct-care compensation, phased to 2030) still on the books as of Nov 2026 with industry lobbying for repeal; labor pool cited as main constraint on HCBS.
excerpt: Paraphrase: 80/20 rule finalized in 2024; limited labor pool is main hindrance to delivering HCBS.
limitations: Trade press; repeal status uncertain.

title: Nurse Agency Licensing Act; Public Act 104-0343 (eff. 15 Aug 2025)
claim: Agencies placing nurses/CNAs in health care facilities must be licensed by IDOL; 2025 amendments expanded investigation/enforcement of unlicensed agencies; rules amended Apr 2025 (68 Ill. Adm. Code 690); fee set by rule.
excerpt: Paraphrase: Department must investigate any nurse agency operating or advertising without a license.
limitations: Fee amount and amended rule text not retrieved.

title: R1 RCM 10-K fiscal 2023
claim: Incumbent RCM economics: 2023 net services revenue $2,254.2M; adjusted EBITDA $614.3M (~27% margin); GAAP net income $3.3M. R1 was later taken private (2024).
excerpt: Paraphrase: net services revenue $2,254.2 million (+24.8%); Adjusted EBITDA $614.3 million.
limitations: Hospital-enterprise RCM with offshore scale; not comparable to a small physician-billing shop; adjusted EBITDA is non-GAAP.

organization: eCFR / Cornell LII (42 CFR 424.73); AAPC and HBMA commentary
title: 42 CFR 424.73 Prohibition of assignment of claims by providers (billing agent exception)
claim: Medicare payment to a billing agent is allowed only if agent compensation is not related to dollars billed or collected; percentage-of-collections fees are defensible only where payment goes directly to the provider's account (AAPC; HBMA RCM Advisor Jan-Feb 2026 flags compliance risk).
excerpt: Paraphrase: agent's compensation must not be related in any way to the dollar amounts billed or collected.
limitations: Interpretive commentary secondary; some state Medicaid programs (e.g., NY MFCU) stricter; Illinois Medicaid stance not verified.

organization: Henry Schein, Inc. (Form 10-K FY2025; Q4 2025 results)
title: Henry Schein 10-K fiscal 2025 and Q4 2025 earnings summaries
claim: Incumbent dental/medical distribution economics: Q4 2025 consolidated gross margin ~30.9%, adjusted operating margin ~7.4%; distribution segment margins lower than manufactured specialty products.
excerpt: We realize substantially higher gross margin from products we develop and manufacture within our Global Specialty Products segment
limitations: Q4 margins from third-party summaries of earnings release; consolidated figures include higher-margin manufacturing and software, so pure distribution margin is lower.

title: Remanufacturing of Medical Devices - final guidance (May 2024)
claim: FDA distinguishes servicing (restoring to original specifications) from remanufacturing (significant change to performance/safety/intended use); remanufacturers face registration, listing, premarket and MDR obligations; FDA continues to defer enforcement on third-party servicing.
excerpt: Paraphrase: guidance helps clarify whether activities performed on devices are likely remanufacturing, with a flowchart and examples.
limitations: Guidance is non-binding; enforcement posture could change; ISO activities need case-by-case analysis.

title: Biosafety Cabinet Field Certifier Accreditation
claim: NSF accreditation for BSC field certifiers requires diploma, 5-day training course, ~1 year of field certification work evidenced by 20 test reports (5 on Class B cabinets), written (3.5h) + practical (8h) exams with own calibrated equipment, ongoing minimum annual test counts; fees by inquiry.
excerpt: Paraphrase: eligibility requires one year of active field certification work shown by twenty test reports.
limitations: Eligibility text partly from older policy quoted by third parties; fees not public.

title: PIMW Transporter requirements
claim: PIMW hauling permit $2,000/yr + $250/vehicle; per-pickup manifests ($4 each), multi-stop manifests not allowed; transport within 10 days; deliver only to permitted facilities; quarterly transport fee per pound (page cites both 1.5c and 3c); exemptions for own-waste transport, noncommercial <50 lb at a time, and USPS.
excerpt: Noncommercial transportation of less than 50 pounds of PIMW at any one time
limitations: Page internally inconsistent on per-pound fee; insurance requirements not stated.

organization: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
title: Handbook for Providers of Transportation Services (issued March 2024)
claim: NEMT enrollment: vehicles licensed by IL Secretary of State (medicars billing stretcher also IDPH-licensed); drivers/attendants must complete HFS-approved safety training every 3 years (payments recouped if not documented); fingerprint-based background checks; OIG on-site visits; enrollment not transferable on change of ownership (new TIN).
excerpt: Failure to produce the documentation upon request from the Department will result in recovery of all payments made
limitations: March 2024 version; HFS issued a further safety-training notice 13 Mar 2026 not reviewed; rates in separate fee schedule.

title: HIPAA business associate contract requirements
claim: Any billing, credentialing, IT, records, courier or other vendor handling PHI for a covered entity must sign a business associate agreement covering permitted uses, safeguards (Security Rule), breach reporting, subcontractor flow-down, HHS access, return/destruction of PHI.
excerpt: Not use or further disclose the information other than as permitted or required by the contract
limitations: Federal baseline only; Illinois-specific privacy laws (e.g., BIPA for biometrics) not reviewed; 2025 HIPAA Security Rule NPRM status not verified.

title: Who Must Register, List and Pay the Fee (medical device establishments)
claim: Domestic wholesale distributors that do not manufacture, repackage, process or relabel are not required to register/list/pay; initial importers must register and pay; repackagers/relabelers and remanufacturers must register, list and pay.
excerpt: Paraphrase: Wholesale Distributor - NO for register, list and pay fee (807.20(c)).
limitations: Servicers not addressed on this page (see remanufacturing guidance); fee amount not listed here.

title: DOT urine collector training requirements
claim: DOT collectors need qualification training plus five consecutive error-free mock collections observed by a qualified trainer; refresher every 5 years; error-correction training within 30 days after a collector-caused cancellation. No state professional license required by this rule.
excerpt: five consecutive error-free mock collections
limitations: Federal DOT rule only; Illinois rules for non-DOT testing not reviewed.

title: Anti-Kickback Statute safe harbor for group purchasing organizations
claim: Vendor fees to a GPO are protected if the GPO has written agreements with members stating vendor fees are 3% or less of purchase price (or specifying amounts) and discloses fees received annually to provider members; GPO cannot be wholly owned by its members.
excerpt: 3 percent or less of the purchase price
limitations: Applies where federal health program reimbursement is involved; dental/vet purchasing largely outside federal programs, so commercial norms rather than AKS govern much of it.

title: Medicare DMEPOS supplier standards
claim: Medicare DMEPOS suppliers need a $50,000 surety bond per enrollment/location (more for adverse legal history), accreditation by a CMS-approved organization, a public location of at least 200 sq ft open at least 30 hours/week, and at least $300,000 liability insurance.
excerpt: Paraphrase: $50,000 base surety bond; at least 200 square feet; open at least 30 hours per week; $300,000 liability policy.
limitations: Regulatory text current as hosted by LII; does not cover competitive bidding contract requirements.

title: DEA registration categories and fees
claim: DEA registration fees: distributing $1,850/yr; reverse distributing $1,850/yr; manufacturing $3,699/yr; practitioner dispensing $888 per 3 years. Distributing controlled substances (e.g., to dental/vet clinics) needs its own DEA registration plus state controlled-substance licensing.
excerpt: Paraphrase: Distributing (Schedules I-V) $1,850, 1 year; Dispensing or instructing $888, 3 years.
limitations: Fee table only; DEA security/recordkeeping obligations and Illinois IDFPR controlled-substance licensing not reviewed.

title: Summary of Infection Prevention Practices in Dental Settings: Basic Expectations for Safe Care
claim: CDC recommends a spore test (biological indicator) at least weekly to monitor dental sterilizers and with every load containing implantable devices; sharps containers disposed of per federal/state/local regulated medical waste rules.
excerpt: A spore test should be used at least weekly to monitor sterilizers.
limitations: CDC guidance, not itself law; enforceability in Illinois depends on dental board rules/standard of care (not verified).

title: Minimum Wage Law
claim: Illinois minimum wage $15.00/hr (18+), sets the floor for caregiver/aide/driver wages; overtime at 1.5x after 40 hrs (home care live-in and overtime costs matter).
excerpt: Paraphrase: $15.00 per hour for workers 18 and older; overtime after 40 hours.
limitations: Chicago and Cook County have higher local minimums (not retrieved); actual market caregiver wages higher than minimum (not retrieved - BLS OEWS page inaccessible).

title: Patterson Companies 10-K fiscal year ended 27 April 2024
claim: Incumbent economics: Dental segment net sales $2,489M with operating income $210M (~8.4%); Animal Health net sales $4,067M with operating income $139M (~3.4%). Dental market 'highly fragmented'; ~202,000 U.S. dentists; 70,000+ private-practice veterinarians (US+Canada); competitors Henry Schein, Benco, Burkhart; MWI/Cencora, Covetrus, Amazon, Chewy.
excerpt: The dental supply market we serve consists of geographically dispersed and highly fragmented dental practices.
limitations: Last 10-K before Patterson went private; segment operating income after corporate allocations; incumbent scale economics.

title: Home Services Agency FAQ
claim: Applicants review 77 IAC 245, Health Care Worker Background Check Code (77 IAC 955) and dementia training code (77 IAC 973); provisional license valid 240 days; IDPH on-site licensure survey within 30 days before provisional expiry; decision on provisional license within ~90 days; separate license/fee per license type (home services vs placement vs nursing).
excerpt: Paraphrase: approval or denial of provisional licensure should take no more than 90 days from submission.
limitations: FAQ does not state worker training hours, administrator qualifications or insurance requirements (77 IAC 245 text not retrievable: ilga.gov returned 503).

title: Stericycle 10-K fiscal 2023 (last full year before acquisition by WM)
claim: Incumbent medical-waste economics: 2023 gross profit $1,014.6M = 38.2% of revenue; markets 'highly competitive on pricing and barriers to entry are low'; competitors include national, regional and local collectors (some collect/transport only); $295.0M small-quantity (SQ) customer class-action settlement over alleged unauthorized/excessive price increases (incl. Illinois Consumer Fraud Act claims); no customer >2% of revenue.
excerpt: The industries and markets in which we operate are highly competitive on pricing and barriers to entry are low.
limitations: Consolidated incl. shredding (Shred-it); incumbent with treatment plants and route density; later acquired (2024), so no newer filings.

organization: Accendra Health, Inc. (f/k/a Owens & Minor; SEC Form 10-K FY2025)
title: Accendra Health 10-K fiscal 2025
claim: Owens & Minor sold its Products & Healthcare Services distribution business for $375M (closed 31 Dec 2025) and renamed itself Accendra Health, keeping home-based patient businesses (Apria, Byram): 2025 net revenue $2.762B (diabetes $783M, sleep $740M, home respiratory $433M, ostomy $213M, wound $189M, urology $116M); revenues depend on Medicare, Medicaid, MA plans and commercial payors; Medicare DMEPOS competitive bidding cut reimbursement in prior rounds; a commercial payor terminated contracts in late 2025.
excerpt: Medicare contracts may be subject to a Competitive Bidding Process (CBP) for durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies
limitations: Margins not extracted; incumbent at national scale with payer contracts a newcomer cannot get.

organization: USASpending.gov (federal contract awards; keyword 'biological safety cabinet', FY24-FY26 window)
title: Federal awards for BSC / fume hood / pharmacy cleanroom certification
claim: Small private certifiers win multi-year federal certification contracts: e.g., Technical Safety Services $214,055 (VA, 2024-2027, BSC/hood/pharmacy clean-room certification, PIID 36C25924P1395); Winergy LLC $202,440 (VA, 2025-2027, pharmacy BSC + room certification + monthly sampling, 36C25625P0797); Health Systems Sciences $174,903 (VA, 2022-2027, 36C25923P0221); Pure Air Testing $125,100 (USDA, 2026-2027).
excerpt: PHARMACY BIOLOGICAL SAFETY CABINET CERTIFICATION, ROOM CERTIFICATION, AND MONTHLY SAMPLING
limitations: Federal facilities only; values are award ceilings/obligations over multi-year periods, not annual revenue; per-unit pricing not shown.

organization: USASpending.gov (keyword 'medical waste', place of performance IL)
title: Federal regulated medical waste awards in Illinois (VA facilities)
claim: Illinois VA medical-waste work is won by smaller firms, not only Stericycle: NEIE Medical Waste Services $335,150 6-month bridge (Jesse Brown VA, 2025, 36C25225N0208) and multiple Hines/Illiana/Lovell orders ($100-294k each); American Vet Solutions $153,452 Hines VA priced period 2026 (36C25226N0190); Daniels Sharpsmart $241,720 (2021-22).
excerpt: REGULATED MEDICAL WASTE AND SHARPS COLLECTION AND DISPOSAL SERVICES FOR THE EDWARD HINES, JR
limitations: Large-quantity hospital generators, unlike the small-generator route model; some VA awards are veteran-owned set-asides (founder status unknown).

title: Federal awards for surgical instrument repair/sharpening
claim: Independent instrument-repair firms hold sizable multi-year VA/DoD contracts: American Surgical Instrument Repair LLC $2,557,500 (VA OH, 2020-2025), $835,800 (VA FL, 2025-2027), $727,680 (DoD tool sharpening); Trillamed LLC $1,260,406 (VA CA, 2024-2027) and $882,160 for 'mobile van on-site surgical instruments repair' (2018-19).
excerpt: MOBILE VAN ON-SITE SURGICAL INSTRUMENTS REPAIR REFURBISHMENT
limitations: Hospital-system scale contracts; small clinics/ASCs/dental/vet buy in much smaller tickets; margins not disclosed.

title: Federal awards for pipette calibration services
claim: Pipette calibration is bought as a recurring service: NovaMed Inc (Illinois place of performance) $284,070 HHS BioWatch 2023-2026; The Pipette Solution LLC $203,375 (HHS 2026-27) and $154,910 (GLP environment); The Scale People $134,528 for annual calibration of ~1,100 pipettes (HHS 2020-2025) - implies roughly $25 per pipette-year [E derived]; Transcat $366,206 (DoD 2021-2026).
excerpt: ANNUAL PIPETTE CALIBRATION SERVICES FOR APPROXIMATELY ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED (1,100) MECHANICAL
limitations: Per-pipette price is our derivation from award total/period and may include repairs; federal pricing tends to be competitive.

title: Federal awards for dental handpiece repair
claim: Handpiece repair tickets are small: HMC Dental Handpiece Repair $50,967 (IHS 2022-2027); 3T Business Group $39,985 (VA base year 2025-26); KaVo (OEM) $17-36k per year at IHS.
excerpt: DENTAL HANDPIECE REPAIR SERVICES
limitations: Federal clinics only; indicates small per-site spend; OEM competes directly.

title: Federal awards for medical equipment repair/maintenance
claim: Multi-vendor medical equipment repair is purchased from ISOs as well as OEMs: Agiliti Health $7.16M (DoD 2023-2026); ServeStrong Solutions LLC $3.86M base+4 (VA 2024-2027); Laparoscopic Technologies (endoscope repair) ~$0.84-0.86M/yr (VA MN); Stryker OEM $0.99M.
excerpt: MEDICAL EQUIPMENT REPAIR SERVICE BASE+4
limitations: Hospital-scale; small-clinic market economics not shown.

title: Federal awards for lab specimen courier services
claim: Small courier firms win VA lab-specimen courier contracts (All American Express Solutions $68,123 4-month bridge Philadelphia VAMC 2024; $20,800/yr Delaware; Crosstown Courier $14,731 2-month bridge), while Quest bundles courier into reference-lab contracts.
excerpt: LAB SPECIMEN COURIER SERVICES
limitations: Few awards; private lab/pharmacy courier rates not shown.

title: Federal purchases of sharps mail-back kits and drug-testing collections
claim: Sharps mail-back kits are bought as catalog products through dental distributors (Darby Dental Supply DLA orders of 1.2-3 gallon mail-back 4-packs, $158-$1,392 per order, 2024-2026); a nationwide DOJ drug-testing collections order to Pembrooke Occupational Health was $51,615 (FY22).
excerpt: SHARPS MAIL BACK , 1.2 GALLON 4-PACK
limitations: Order quantities not shown, so unit prices cannot be derived; few awards.
